Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 
Kabc020131682021 
In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor
Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small
 Causes Bengaluru
 (Scch-18)
 Dated: This the 22nd day of January 2024
 Present: V.Nagamani
 B.A.L., Ll.B., Ll.M.,
 Iii Addl. Judge &
 Member, Mact
 Court Of Small Causes,
 Bengaluru.
 M.V.C. No.2049/2021
 Petitioner Shri Yashawantha B.V.,
 Son of Venkateshappa,
 Aged about 19 years,
 Residing at Bandarlahalli,
 Chintamani Taluk,
 Chikkaballapura District.
 (By Pleader Shri
 C.N.Sonnappa)
 V/s
 Respondents 1.Shri Narasimhappa,
Son of Gangappa, Residing at Diguru Village, Kagathi Post, Chintamani Taluk, Chickballapura
District. 
(Exparte)
2.The Iffco -Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd., Sri Shanthi Towers, 5th Floor, No.141, 3rd Main
East of Ngef, Kasturinagar, Bengaluru-560 043.
(By Pleader Kiran Pujar) *J U D G M E N T * This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident. 
*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
1 2. It is forthcoming in the petition averments that, on the fateful date of the accident, on 17.12.2020 at about 7.15 p.m, the petitioner was riding his Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-51-D-3505 slowly and cautiously on Chinnasandra-Hirekattigenahalli road by wearing helmet, when he reached near Channakeshavapura Gate, Chintamani Taluk, at that time, a Tractor bearing registration No.KA- 52-T-3216 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner. Consequently, the petitioner had sustained severe injuries. 
3. It is stated that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Government Hospital,
Chintamani for first aid treatment, he was referred to Gaurav Orthopedics and surgical hospital,
Kolar, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient. The petitioner had spent Rs.8,00,000/- towards his medical and travelling expenses. 
4. It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 19 years, doing work as a carpenter and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month, and used to contribute the entire earnings, for the maintenance of the family. Due to the severe injuries, he became permanently disabled person. 
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident in question had taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor bearing registration No.KA-52-T-3216. In this regard,
case was registered in Crime No.462/2020 against the driver of the offending vehicle. As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.2, being the insurance company, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation, to the petitioner. 
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition for compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- against the respondents. 
6. After registration of the case, as usual, notices were issued to the respondents. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1, remained absent, placed exparte as per the order of this court. On the other hand, the respondent No.2, has made his appearance through its counsel and filed written statement in answer to the case of the petitioner. 
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.2, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, seriously disputed about the involvement of the offending vehicle, and also the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle. But, admitted the issuance of insurance policy, and its validity, as on the date of the accident. It is alleged that, the driver of the Tractor had no valid and effective driving license, to drive the said vehicle. It is also the contention of the respondent No.2 that, neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S.134(c) and S.158(6) of the M.V. Act, by furnishing the better particulars. It is another contention of this respondent that, due to the sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, accident and its consequences were taken place. Hence, the owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-51-Q- 3505 are the necessary parties to the proceedings. With all these grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against the respondent company. 
Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
2 8. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case,
following issues were framed:
*I S S U E S*
1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 17.12.2020 at about 7.15 p.m. near Channakeshavapura Gate, Chintamani Taluk, Chickballapur District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor bearing registration No.KA-52-T- 3216 in an actionable negligence? 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate? From whom?
3. What order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner-Yashawanth B.V. relied on his affidavit evidence, by stepping into the witness box and was examined as PW1. Subsequently, additional affidavit also been filed. At the time of his evidence, 30 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P21 and Ex.P28 to Ex.P36, Ex.P40 to Ex.P51. Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Medical Record Technicians by name M.B. Srinivas and R.Agilasithan as PW2 & PW3. At the time of their evidence, 4 documents got marked as Ex.P22 to Ex.P25. In addition to this, relied on the evidence of Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW4. At the time of his evidence 2 documents got marked as Ex.P26 & Ex.P27. Further examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW5. At the time of his evidence placed Ex.P37 to Ex.P39, for consideration. 
10. On the other hand, the respondent No.2, to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statement, has examined PSI of Nandagudi Police Station by name Subramanya V. as RW1. Further examined Assistant Manager of Legal of the insurance company by name Nagendra R. as RW2. 
Thereafter examined official of the R.T.O. office, Nelamangala by name U.Manjunath as RW3. At the time of his evidence placed Ex.R1 & Ex.R2, for consideration. 
11. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner and perused the materials available on record. At the time of arguments the counsel for the petitioner has relied the following authorities; 1) MFA No.103196/2018 between Somappa Balappa Nandi & Mallappa & Another 2)
2022 ACJ 1427 between Gopalappa Vs. Kandaluru Shankar Reddy & Another 3) 2021 ACJ 1824 between Irshad Hassan Vs. Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd., 4) MFA 1245/2010 (MV) between United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Narasappa & Another 12. With due respect, I have gone through the propositions laid down in the said authority, on the point of assessment of compensation in the injury case, on different heads, by appreciating the medical documents and the nature of the injuries, sustained by the victim of social legislation. 
Further, it was observed in the last authority that, non- registration of the vehicle as on the date of Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
3 the accident cannot be a ground to deny the compensation by the insurance company. 
13. On the other hand, the counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied the following authorities 1) ILR 2009 KAR 3562 between Veerappa & Another Vs. Siddappa & Another 2) MFA 3475/2008 (MVC) between Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. B.C.Kumar & Another 14. With due respect, I have gone through the propositions laid down in the said cases, on the point that Fraud and justice never dwell together. Further, observed that, false case filed by the claimant ought have been taken note by the MACT, and the claim petition ought to have been dismissed. 
15. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, I answered the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
16. The petitioner herein, has to prove the direct nexus between the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, Tractor bearing registration No.KA-52-T-3216 and the grievous injuries sustained by him, due to the said actionable negligence. Since, the burden to prove the above issue, is on the petitioner, on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities. 
17. It is pertinent to note that, the respondent No1, being the owner of the offending vehicle, without challenging the case of the petitioner remained as silent spectator herein. The respondent No.2 being the insurance company, though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, even denied the factum of involvement of the offending vehicle, in the accident. In such a situation, careful scrutiny of th evidence placed by both the parties, on record, is necessary herein, for effective adjudication of the case. 
18. To discharge the burden lies on the petitioner Yashawanth B.V. relied on his affidavit evidence and examined as PW1. Apart from this, he relied on his additional affidavit, with respect to his subsequent treatment. Among the documentary evidence placed by him, in support of the above issue, Ex.P1 to Ex.P7, Ex.40 to Ex.51 are the material documents for consideration. Remaining documents and evidence of PW2 to PW5 are to be considered in detail, at the time of discussion of issue No.2.
19. In the affidavit evidence of PW1, reiterated the main petition averments about the accident as well as actionable negligence said to have committed by the driver of the offending vehicle, which caused accident and its consequences.
20. On the other hand, the respondent company, had placed the evidence of the investigation officer, who filed charge sheet in the criminal case, pertaining to the present accident in question, by Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/ 
4 name Subramany V was examined as RW1. In the evidence of the said witness, deposed about his investigation process from the registration of the case, on the basis of first information, till filing of the final report. At the time of his evidence, no documentary evidence placed on record, for consideration. 
21. Apart from this, placed the evidence of RW2- Nagendra R. The said witness, being the Assistant manager of the company, in support of the defenses forthcoming in the written statement, deposed that, after 3 days of the alleged accident, first information was given against the unknown vehicle. 
Thereafter, the petitioner, in collusion with the police officials, and owner of the offending vehicle,
false case has been foisted against the driver of the offending vehicle, by implicating the said vehicle,
in order to wangle an award. Hence, the petition filed by the claimant is not tenable under law, and the same are liable to be dismissed. In support of the said defense, no documentary evidence placed on record, for consideration. 
22. Another witness from the side of the company, U. Manjunath being the FDA of R.T.O, at the time o his evidence, had placed Authorisation letter and B extract as per Ex.R1 and Ex.R2 by stating that, as per the Ex.R2, offending vehicle was resisted on 30.03.2021. Except this, no whisper in his evidence about the accident. 
23. On taking birds eye view towards the documentary evidence Ex.P1 reflect that, alleged accident had taken palace on 17.12.2020. On the basis of first information given by the father of the petitioner on 20.12.2020, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle, by name Narasimhappa, alleging that, he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC. After registration of the case, by mentioning the name of the driver of the offending vehicle, immediately after the registration of the case, either the owner or its driver had not questioned these two material documents, to disprove the involvement of the offending vehicle, as well as to disprove the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
24. Another material point of delay in giving first information is concerned, in the recitals of Ex.P1,
column No.3(c) and also in the recitals of Ex.P2 , the father of the petitioner, clearly narrated that,
since he was providing treatment to his son, belated complaint was given. When the petitioner had sustained injuries in the accident, one cannot expect immediate complaint without providing treatment to his son. To suspect about the case of the petitioner, on the point of delay of 3 days, no convincing contra materials available from the side of the respondent company. Hence delay is not fatal to the case of the petitioner, and on the point of delay, entire case of the petitioner, cannot be thrown out. 
25. Added to this, on perusal of the spot mahazar dated 21.12.2020 executed in the presence of panch witnesses Ex.P4 vehicle seizure mahazar dated 12.4.2021 along with Ex.P5 Motor Vehicle Inspector report, go to show about the involvement of the offending vehicle. At the time of argument, learned counsel for the respondent company, highlighted the point that, the offending vehicle was seized after four months of the accident in question. To this point, in the recitals of Ex.P4, it is evident that, the said mahazar process had conducted in the premises of Chintamani Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
5 Rural Police Station. As on the date of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle, ran away from the spot along with the vehicle, subsequently, through the police official H.C. 249, Sandeep Kumar, the offending vehicle was detected and seized in the presence of panch witnesses. At the time of seizure of the said vehicle, either the owner or its driver were not opposed the said seizure process, at all the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident. 
26. As per the report of the inspector, alleged accident was not due to the mechanical defects of the vehicle involved in the accident. Though there was no damage to the tractor and trailer as per the said document, the damages noted in connection with the defending vehicle, clearly depict about due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle accident in question had taken place. Another material document Ex.P6 wound certificate of the petitioner reveals that, on 17.12.2020 at about 7.15 p.m. there was an accident between two wheeler and tractor. On the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries. Apart from this, on going through the statement of the victim Yeshawanth witness Nagesh, Krishnappa clearly speak about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, on perusal of Ex.P42 and Ex.P43 police notice and reply to the police notice, statement of the driver of the offending vehicle, seizure mahazar and idemnity bond executed in the criminal court, list of property sent to the Magistrate along with the certified copy of the seized offending and defending vehicles marked at Ex.P44 to Ex.P50 depict about the genuineness of the case of the petitioner. To eradicate the recitals of all these documents no contra materials available on record from the side of the company except canvasing the point of non-involvement of the offending vehicle as well as in connection with the seizure of the offending vehicle. 
27. It is relevant to note that, when the respondent company is strongly disputing on the point of delay, as well as the involvement of the offending vehicle, company could have appoint the investigating agency from the side of the company, to get the genuine report about the accident to disprove the case of the petitioner in the case on hand. Another, material document Ex.P51 goes to show that, after registration of the criminal case against the driver of the offending vehicle, the said driver appeared before the court and obtained bail. The said case is pending for final determination. 
28. Ultimately, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer reveals that,
after due investigation process final report has been filed against the driver of the offending vehicle by name Narasimhappa alleging that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 388 of IPC and also 187 of 192 of the M.V. Act. As per the allegation forthcoming in the column NO.17 of the charge sheet, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle accident had taken place. In the said accident petitioner had sustained grievous injuries. At the time of accident without number plate offending vehicle was plying on the road by its driver. The recitals of the charge sheet and also the recitals of the Ex.P51 remained unshaken by the other side. 
29. At the time of cross-examination of PW1 learned counsel for the respondent company, in para No.2, put several suggestions and questions with respect to the manner of the accident, and also in para No.4, questioned on the point of delay and about involvement of the offending vehicle. But,
nothing has been elicited to disprove the case of the petitioner against the driver of the offending vehicle. Even at the time of further cross-examination of PW1, questions put to the witness about Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
6 non- involvement of the offending vehicle has been clearly denied by the PW1.
30. On the other hand, at the time of cross- examination of RW1, by the learned counsel for the respondent company, after treating this witnesses as hostile, put several questions on the point of delay in seizure of offending vehicle, and about involvement of the offending vehicle, as well as registration certificate pertaining to the offending vehicle, on appreciation of the answers given by the RW1 in toto, clearly evident about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, as well as allegations of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle. At the time of cross-examination of RW1, by the learned counsel for the petitioner clearly admitted that,
after service of 133 notice, no counter complaint received and due process final report has been filed and also received necessary document from the RTO. The RW2, at the time of cross-examination admitted that, in the PF chassis number of the offending vehicle has been mentioned. Further he admitted that Narasimhappa has not given any statement to the effect that, offending vehicle is not involved in the accident. Further, he admitted that, in connection with the engine and chassis of the offending vehicle, they issued policy. 
31. Over all appreciation of the police documents along with the evidence of PW1, RW1 & RW2, it is crystal clear that evidence given by the PW2 is prevails over the evidence of the respondent company, in connection with the above fact in issue. Hence, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed cogent and convincing evidence for consideration. 
32. In the light of the evidence placed on record, by way of affidavit evidence and the documentary evidence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioner has successfully proved the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle Tractor bearing registration No.KA-52-T- 3216. Hence,
without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1, in the Affirmative. 
ISSUE NO.2 :
33. This issue is with respect to the entitlement of relief claimed by the petitioner. The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads. 
34. Before discussion of the evidence placed by the petitioner, in support of the above issue, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act. 
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another. 
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant. The compensation should not be assessed conservatively. On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavour to secure some uniformity and consistency. The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
7 money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner." 
35. In the light of the preposition laid down in the above case, let me to discuss the evidence available on record. Prior to that, it is relevant to note that, "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable. That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment. But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation. "
36. In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, relied on wound certificate marked at Ex.P6. In Ex.P6, forthcoming following injuries:-
1) Tenderness, swelling, deformity of right knee and upper 1/3rd of right leg 2) Foot drop right foot 37. As per the opinion of the doctor, the injury Nos.1 & 2 are grievous in nature. Apart from this, the petitioner has produced, discharge summaries, as per Ex.P9, & Ex.P16, assessment reports as per Ex.P10, photographs as per Ex.P11, CD as per Ex.P12, medical bills as per Ex.P13 & Ex.P17,
prescriptions as per Ex.P14 and x-ray as per Ex.P15 & Ex.P21, deposit receipt, requisition slip as per Ex.P18 to Ex.P20. The petitioner through his additional affidavit has produced discharge summaries, photographs, CD, medical bills, quotation bill, advance receipts, prescriptions and X-rays as per Ex.P28 to Ex.P36. Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Medical record keeper by name M.G. Srinivas and R.Agilasithan as PW2 & PW3. They have placed inpatient records along with authorisation letters as per Ex.P22 to Ex.P25. Further examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. and Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW4 & PW5. They have placed clinical note, x-ray, inpatient record, clinical notes and x-ray as per Ex.P26, Ex.P27, Ex.P37 to Ex.P39.
38. On going through the discharge summary of Gaurav Orthopaedics & Surgical Hospital as per Ex.P9, the petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient from 17.12.2020 to 31.12.2020, 3.3.2021 to 14.3.2021 and 20.9.2021 to 28.9.2021. Another discharge summary reveals that he was admitted to Akash Medical Sciences & Research Centre from 21.2.2022 to 12.5.2022. Further, he has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P28 of Akash Hospital reveals that, he was admitted on 4.7.2022 to 23.7.2022. Again he has produced another discharge summary goes to show that, he was admitted to Sanjaygandhi Hospital from 1.12.2022 to 8.12.2022. For having taken note of the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, and his sufferings at the time of taking treatment, in connection with the aforesaid grievous injuries, I am of the view that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering. 
39. Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period is concerned, on going through the main petition, his avocation has been mentioned as carpenter and was getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month. There is no iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner as Rs.20,000/- per month. On going through the discharge Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
8 summary of Gaurav Orthopaedics & Surgical Hospital as per Ex.P9, the petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient from 17.12.2020 to 31.12.2020, 3.3.2021 to 14.3.2021 and 20.9.2021 to 28.9.2021. Another discharge summary reveals that he was admitted to Akash Medical Sciences &
Research Centre from 21.2.2022 to 12.5.2022. Further he has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P28 of Akash Hospital reveals that, he was admitted on 4.7.2022 to 23.7.2022. Again he has produced another discharge summary goes to show that, he was admitted to Sanjaygandhi Hospital from 1.12.2022 to 8.12.2022. 
40. On going through the nature of the injuries sustained by him, reveal that, he could have taken treatment as an inpatient as well as an outpatient at least for a period of six months. During this period, on going through his occupation forthcoming in the main petition, averments as well as in the evidence of PW1, he was not in a position to do any work. Hence, I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.87,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period. 
41. The petitioner herein, in connection with his treatment expenses, at the time of his evidence,
placed medical bills of Rs.3,59,210/-, Rs.3,857/- & Rs.12,348/- as per Ex.P13, Ex.P17 and Ex.P32 along prescriptions as per Ex.P14 & Ex.P35 and advance receipts as per Ex.P34. Other side not seriously disputed the medical bills except the suggestion that, they are created bills for the sake of getting more compensation. At the time of further cross-examination he clearly narrated about the dates on which he had been treated as an inpatient. by taking into consideration of all these aspects will not give an access to suspect about the genuineness of the medical bills submitted by the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,75,415/- towards medical expenses. 
42. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, had sustained grievous injuries fully mentioned above. As per the records, for his injuries, he took treatment in Gaurav Orthopaedics &
Surgical Hospital from 17.12.2020 to 31.12.2020, 3.3.2021 to 14.3.2021 and 20.9.2021 to 28.9.2021. 
Further Akash Medical Sciences & Research Centre from 21.2.2022 to 12.5.2022. from 4.7.2022 to 23.7.2022. Again he was treated in Sanjaygandhi Hospital from 1.12.2022 to 8.12.2022. During this period of treatment, the petitioner could have taken the assistance of the attendant, and he could have spent some amount towards travelling, food and nourishment. Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges. 
43. Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him. In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence, along with the wound certificate. 
In the evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition. As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6, goes to show that, he had sustained the injuries, fully mentioned in the wound certificate, which shows the grievous nature of the injuries. In connection with these injuries, the petitioner has placed discharge summaries and x-rays and also the medical records pertaining to the various Hospitals. In addition to this, placed the evidence of PW2 and PW3 who produced the medical documents of the petitioner. Apart from this,
Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
9 the petitioner had placed the evidence of the doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj B.N. & Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW4 & PW5.
44. In the evidence of this material witness, PW4-Dr.Nagaraj B.N. deposed that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained closed tromatic right proximal tibia comminuted fracture with impending compartment syndrome with right foot drop. In this regard, the petitioner was treated initially at Government hospital, Chintamani later at Gourav Orthopaedic Hospital. Wherein he underwent fasciotomy fort release of compartment syndrome with ORIF for the right tibia with LCP. 
Later underwent wound debridement excision of non-viable muscles with SSG for the right leg and advise for follow-up treatment. Once again underwent implant removal and ortho fix with DAC dressing. Thereafter, admitted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital with non-union of right tibia later got admitted to Sanjaygandhi Hospital with the complaint of non- union of right proximal of dead bone with primary closure, there after admitted to Akash hospital with loss of sensation and unable to dorsiflexion of right ankle where he was diagnosed as post tromatic right leg foot drop with soft tissue contractures with equinus deformity. In this regard, he underwent ankle orthodesis with IMIL nail, tendo achilies. Once again, got admitted to Akash hospital on the complaint of pain and he was treated conservatively. 
45. It is also forthcoming that, when the petitioner had approached the PW4 for assessment of disability on the basis of clinical and radiological examination, PW4 has noticed that, the petitioner walks with walker with equinus gait, shortening of right lower limb by 4 cms, discharging wound present over the right ankle. Further, on the basis of x-ray of the right ankle shown fused right ankle with implants in situ. Further PW4 deposed that, on the basis of stability components, mobility components and also by considering x-ray points came to the conclusion that, the physical disability of the right lower limb of the petitioner is at 75%, wholebody physical disability is 25%. Further opined that, the petitioner needs regular dressing for the healing of the right ankle wound and advised for below knee amputation. In support of the evidence of PW4 placed clinical note and x-ray as per Ex.P26 & Ex.P27.
46. On the other hand, in the evidence of PW5 Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. deposed that, on examination of the petitioner on 13.10.2022 he noticed, infected right ankle orthodisis with implant in situ. In this regard, he underwent multiple surgeries in different hospitals and later below knee amputation was done in their hospital on 3.12.2022. On 22.5.2023 he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability, at that time, he noticed on the basis of clinical and radiological examination about,
amputation for right knee upper 1/3rd. After assessing the disability on the point of mobility and stability components by giving extra points, came to the conclusion that whole body disability is 75%
which is permanent in nature. further opined that, the petitioner needs artificial limb prosthesis approximate cost of the same is Rs.50,000/- to Rs.1,00,000/-. In support of the evidence of PW5 placed 2 inpatient records with clinical note as per Ex.P37 & Ex.P38.
47. At the time of cross-examination of PW5, admitted that, as per the notification, only affected area disability has to be assessed, and there is no any formula, to assess the whole body disability. 
Generally, for upper and lower limb disability, whole body disability has to be considered by adopting 1/3rd of the particular limb. Further, he admitted that, he has gone through the discharge Yashawanth B.V vs Narasimhappa on 22 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70762857/
10 summary of the petitioner, but gone through the further treatment documents, and he denied the suggestion of the learned counsel for the respondent company, that he assessed the disability in higher side. 
48. It is pertinent note that, after examination- in-chief evidence of PW4 not tendered for cross- examination. Hence, there is no evidentiary value to his evidence as contemplated under evidence Act. On the other hand, on appreciation of evidence of PW5, and by looking into the voluminous medical documents of the petitioner, I am of the view that, due to the amputation of one leg, the petitioner has to suffer a lot in future, and he has to depend upon others, in one or the other way,
